newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore stocks steady, eye regional currencies.
newsitem.headline: Singapore stocks steady, eye regional currencies.

text.p: Singapore stocks were mostly steady at mid-morning on Monday, with banking stocks underpinned by Singapore's pro-financial sector budget, dealers said.
"Banks are benefitting from the budget," said one.

He said the foreign tranches of DBS led the banks, rising Singapore $0.30 to S$19.40 due to its competitive edge in Asian Currency Units activities -- the area Singapore's budget boosts with new incentives.
However, dealers said caution still ruled amid fears of regional currency falls following the Thai baht float and a de facto Philippine peso devaluation.

Malaysia Bank Negara suprised the market early in the day by allowing the ringgit to fall against the U.S. dollar after weeks of supporting it. On Friday, Indonesia's central bank widened its intervention band in the rupiah/dollar.
"People are watching to see if there will be a spillover onto the Singapore dollar," said another local dealer.
The Singapore dollar weakened to trade around 1.4425 to the U.S. dollar from 1.4395 earlier.
While some dealers hoped cheaper currencies would lure foreign funds into the region, others said uncertainty in the area was not helpful.
At 0200 GMT, the Straits Times Industrials Index was up 3.13 points at 1,970.27. The UOB OTC index, which tracks Malaysian shares, was down 3.77 points at 1,098.95.
Mulitmedia Creative Technology rose S$0.30 to S$28.20, reflecting gains in high-tech stocks in the U.S..
Malaysian KLI Holdings eased 18 cents to S$1.64 on top volume of over nine million shares after it announced a 450 million ringgit reverse takeover of Rahman Hydraulic Tin Bhd.
Keppel Corp fell 15 cents to S$6.40 after the company sought to raise S$500 million in funds.
